definition: An AI notetaker is a tool using artificial intelligence to take notes during meetings.
details: They are created by tech companies such as Microsoft and Google; by AI transcription services such Otter.ai, and by smaller firms such as Cluely and Krisp. Some business executives send AI notetakers to attend meetings not only to take notes, but also to answer questions on their behalf. The use of AI notetakers raises ethical questions, including recording meetings without the consent of all participants and the possibility that the notetaker will hallucinate and misrepresent what was said during meetings. There are also concerns when it comes to the privacy and security of meeting data and the sensitive information that lives inside meetings. AI notetakers can also create legal and compliance issues for organizations because meeting recordings and AI-generated transcripts may implicate participant notice and consent, retention, vendor access, biometric data, confidentiality, and attorney-client privilege. Further controversies have developed from the use of AI notetakers such as Cluely to cheat in technical job interviews.

explainer.lead: An AI notetaker turns speech from meetings or other interactions into transcripts, minutes, and follow-up material, reducing the need for someone to take detailed notes. The convenience comes with serious responsibilities: participants may need to consent to recording, sensitive data must be protected, and generated notes can misrepresent what was actually said.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a helper who sits in class, writes down what everyone says, and then prepares a short summary so you can concentrate on the discussion. An AI notetaker does something similar for meetings, but it can make mistakes or even write things that were never said. People should also agree to being recorded, because the conversation may contain private information.
tiers.practitioner: These tools appear as meeting features in productivity platforms and as standalone transcription services, often using cloud processing, web uploads, mobile apps, or browser extensions. Typical outputs include editable, time-aligned transcripts, text or subtitle exports, multilingual transcription, minutes, and agendas. Before deployment, test transcription quality and review outputs for hallucinations; also address participant notice and consent, retention, vendor access, biometric data, confidentiality, and attorney-client privilege.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation, an interaction produces audio or video x, and speech recognition produces a transcript T = f(x); downstream processing derives meeting documentation such as minutes or agendas from T. Implementations may attempt contextual awareness, emotional interpretation, and real-time processing, but these capabilities do not guarantee faithful representation. Known limits include hallucinated or misleading content and legal, privacy, and security risks associated with recordings and generated transcripts.

explainer.example: During a recorded project meeting, an AI notetaker converts the audio into an editable, time-aligned transcript and prepares minutes plus agenda items for the next meeting. Before circulating them, the organizer checks the notes against the recording because the system may have added or distorted information, and confirms that recording consent and organizational data-handling requirements were addressed.

usedIn.name: Cluely

explainer.intuition: The basic idea is to separate participating in a conversation from documenting it. Software handles the recording and transcription work, while people remain responsible for checking the result and deciding whether recording and data handling are appropriate.
howItWorks: Capture live meeting audio or accept an uploaded audio or video recording.
Apply AI-based speech recognition to convert the speech into text.
Produce an editable transcript aligned with times in the recording.
Derive materials such as detailed minutes or agendas for upcoming meetings and deliverables.
Let users edit, review, and export the resulting text or subtitles.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI notetakers can remove routine office work and let participants focus on the discussion, while also making spoken interactions searchable and easier to reuse. Their errors and access to sensitive conversations can affect business decisions, individual privacy, security, legal compliance, and fairness in settings such as technical interviews.
misconceptions: A transcript is not a guaranteed factual record; the system can hallucinate or misrepresent speech.
A notetaker joining a meeting does not by itself establish that everyone consented to recording.
These tools are not limited to live meetings; some process recordings uploaded through web, mobile, or browser interfaces.
